utterances.text: I was present when one was pushed in. What happened before that and after that, I don't know, but the laughter and the screams could be heard for a long time before I looked and after I had looked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Laughter and screams at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, speaking of the people you saw being shot between the "white house" and the "red house," what you call the people from Hambarine, what made you go out at night? Was it allowed for you detainees to go and walk out, or did you hear voices to bring you out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I didn't go out. I just woke up and raised my head a little to look through the window to see what was happening outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And they were not far away from your window. Were they close enough to see the whole incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: The incident was more or less over when I woke up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mean you heard the shots.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Yes. That's what woke me up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: That's what woke you up. And you saw what you said, "when the brains were like milk." You saw that too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Clearly? You could see that clearly from your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I saw that quite clearly, white powder coming out of the head to one side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What part of the night was that? Was it ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: It was after midnight, about 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But there was enough light to see all of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Not for a hundred per cent clear visibility, but the number of people you could see afterwards when they were loaded into the scoop and onto the truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you see the loading too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, also another question concerning what you call the fatal transport to Trnopolje, and you were included in that transport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Did I say fatal for Trnopolje or for Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Well, all right. You said Trnopolje and Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I don't know which transport you want me to comment on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: All right. The transport where they brought people down and they were being killed 50 metres away from the bus. Were you in the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Yes. That happened at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And you saw the killing or you heard the shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: We were all forced to squat on a large field of grass, and then these men were taken some 50 or 60 metres, away from us, next to the buses, which were empty at the moment. Then we heard screams when those men were beaten with various objects. This didn't last long. We had to look to the ground and continue squatting there in that field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: These people were chosen from your bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I don't know who was in my bus that night. But anyway, when we were all taken off the buses, then out of this large crowd of 1.500 people maybe, they were selected from that large group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You have no idea what was the basis of the selection? Was it random or was it lists which were already prepared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I don't know what it was really, but they were mostly well-known persons, businessmen from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mean -- what you call "well-known," is the people among the elite of the society or among the militant who were fighting, if you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: They were not fighters. They were business people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness AM, you said that you actually saw one man, though you didn't recognise him, being thrown into the fire or pushed into the fire. That's right? You could actually --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: -- see only one man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And the next day, you said that you just saw ashes there. You didn't see any burnt corpses or bodies, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Did you see any persons or prisoners walking around with any burns on them, any burnt prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. During the period you were in Omarska, I think over two months or something along those lines, during that period of time, did you get to know any of the people in charge in Omarska, any of the -- you mentioned Marmat as one guard. Did you know any of the other guards or officials by name, nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: I heard from an active-duty policeman that his colleague from work, an active-duty policeman, Kvocka by surname, was for a time the commander, leader, warden, whatever you like, of the camp. Afterwards, he was replaced. According to rumours among people who knew him, he apparently was married to a Muslim, that he tried to protect a certain number of Muslim people, and this was taken against him and he had to leave his position. He was then replaced by another person surnamed Meakic. I didn't know either of them before, nor in the camp, to be able to identify them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. Witness AM, I only have one question for you. Is there something that you would like to say and which still hasn't been asked of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the people who committed crimes in this war, regardless of which ethnicity they belong to, be they Muslim, Serbs, or Croats, to be brought before justice and punished as an example to future generations, for such things not to happen again as happened to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are all here to achieve that goal and we share your wishes. I think there are no exhibits to be tendered. I think that all the exhibits have already been tendered. So I'm going to ask the usher to close the blinds before the witness leaves. Just a moment. Excuse me. Mr. Simic? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in line with the decisions we have taken, I would have two or three questions, because Their Honours, I think Judge Wald, touched a subject that was not touched upon during the examination and cross-examination. So if I may be allowed to ask a couple of additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You need additional information from the witness? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, linked to the question by Her Honour, Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the issue was very lightly mentioned, but all right, please put your question. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AM, in answer to a question by Judge Wald and by Judge Riad, I would have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, only the question of Kvocka, not the question of money; that's over. We discussed the question of money. So the question that you could legitimately ask has to do with the mention of Mr. Kvocka by the witness, only that. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AM, what was the name of the active-duty policeman who gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: Hamdija Arifagic. He was working in Omarska, and his colleague was Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AM
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor. Do you have any additional questions on this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. PIACENTE
utterances.text: No thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now the usher can lower the blinds. Witness, you have finished your testimony. Thank you very much for coming, and we wish you a safe journey to your place of residence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Hollis, if you please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness will testify in open session, and it's Nusret Sivac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the clock, and if we begin now with the testimony, then the break is very shortly. If we have a half-hour break now, then we have another hour and a half to work, which is quite acceptable. So maybe this is a good time to have a break and then we will resume after that, after a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nusret Sivac, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Are you comfortable, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. You're now going to answer questions that will be put to you by Madam Hollis. Madam Hollis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, for the record, would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: My name is Nusret Sivac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth and your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was born on the 19th of August, 1947 in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: From 1973 until 1989, did you work in Prijedor for the police?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. I worked for the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you work in the communications centre?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It was called the centre for communications and crypto-security.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what were your duties there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: That is one of the key departments of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was an operative.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand operative. What exactly did you do?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: In the communications centre, the main area of activity were written communications which were conducted through various types of messages and memoranda. The communication with other Security Services on the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the former Yugoslavia was also carried out through radio communications and special telephone communications which were part of that communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you were one of the operators for that communication. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and english transcripts

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a policeman by the name of Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long had you known him in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I knew him well enough. He came to work for the security service in Prijedor some ten years. That is, I'd known him for about ten years before 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how often would you have contact with him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, as much as I needed to contact him for my work.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know his wife and her family?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I knew her much better than I knew him. He was born on the same street and we grew up together in the same street.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you know her brothers?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew them very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a woman by the name of Slavica Lakic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did she work at the Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. She was a secretary and typist, and she worked at the public security service in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And during the time you worked at the public security service, did you ever see Slavica Lakic and Kvocka come to work together or leave work together?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a policeman by the name of Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I knew him for much longer than I knew Kvocka. I knew him in 1983 when I joined the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sorry, you joined the public security service in 1983 or 1973?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How frequently would you have contact with Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, I would see him as often as I needed to see him for my work, for the work that we did together.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he known by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Krkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man by the name of Drago Prcac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I knew him in 1973, when I came to work for the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, what was his position in the police?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He worked in the crime department. He was a crime technician. He would conduct on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you have contact with him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Very often, as often as the nature of our work required.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time period 1973 to 1989, did you also work as a cameraman for the local television station and sometimes write articles for the local media?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: During that time, did Drago Prcac ever ask you to film programmes about Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, he did, on one or two occasions. Upon his recommendation, we went there and we made a programme about the life and the work of people in the village of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you observe the attitude of the people of that area towards Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The people there, like myself, had a great deal of respect for Drago Prcac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a policeman by the name of Zeljko Meakic.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how long did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I knew him because we worked together for the security service. He worked as a policeman in the police station in Omarska most of that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you leave the police in 1989?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Because of the atmosphere that had been created in the communications centre. In other words, the then chief of the communications centre wanted to cleanse ethnically that most vital part of the security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who was this chief?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The chief was Milos Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you say that he wanted to cleanse this communications centre ethnically. What groups did he want to rid the centre of?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Of Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you left the police and until April of 1992, did you continue to work as a cameraman and sometimes write articles for the local media?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you continue to cover the events that were happening in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Dule Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: We worked together at the security service in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in 1992, if you know, what was his position?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was the police commander in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, if you know, based on your observations, did Mr. Jankovic work in cooperation with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man by the name of Marko Dzenadija?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He too was an employee of the security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was his position in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I think that he was the deputy commander of the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Based on your observations, if you know, did Mr. Dzenadija work in cooperation with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: In 1992, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in 1992, were you married?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have children?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I had two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what were their ages?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: My daughter was 11 and my son was 6 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What property did you have in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I had a large apartment in the very centre of the Prijedor town, and I had a cottage house with a two-hectare orchard some kilometres away from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you also have a vehicle in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had a Ford Escort.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the 10th of June of 1992. Were you arrested on that date?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: By whom were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was arrested by Bato Kovacevic and a reserve policeman whom we referred to as Brkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And were you taken to the SUP and then from there to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What other people were taken to Keraterm with you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Together with me in the police van was a judge from the municipal court in Prijedor, Omer Kerenovic, and a private caterer, Safet Ramadanovic, and Ivica Muntijan was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Ivica Muntijan, what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was a doorman at the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Keraterm, did you hear a list of names being called out?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you know, this list of names was people from what area?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: From Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, after this list of names were called out, were these people and you and the others you have named taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell the Judges what happened when you first arrived in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: When we first arrived in Omarska, we had to undergo the admission procedure of detainees in the camp. We didn't know what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you -- I'm sorry. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Guards approached the police van at one point, and one of them -- later on I heard it was their boss, his name was Krkan -- took a list -- took the list from Tomislav Stojakvic, who had brought us to Omarska, and he ordered the guards to start taking out the people from the rear part of the police van.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And these people that were taken out from the rear part of the police van, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They were lined up against a wall and beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I don't know how, but Miroslav Kvocka appeared. He took the lists that had been handed over to him by Tomislav Stojakovic, the one who had driven us there, and he took the list somewhere in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who was it who gave the list to Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Krle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you testified just a moment ago that when you first arrived, the driver gave a list to a man you later learned was the boss Krkan. Was Krkan there when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I said that Krle had been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: So Krle was there, took the list, and then gave the list to Kvocka when Kvocka appeared; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, once Kvocka got the list, what did Kvocka do?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He went to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Approximately three groups of detainees from Keraterm were taken in groups of three or four. They were lined up against a wall and then beaten with various batons and clubs. Then one by one they were taken to the back part of the camp. I don't know where they were being taken to.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: After that, a guard ordered us to get out of the police van.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And after you got out of the police van, then what happened?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Tomislav Stojakvic handed over the list to Krle again, the list containing our names who were in this last group to have arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Kvocka came. He took the list and again he went to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And after he went to the administration building, then what occurred?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: After that, the guards took us towards the wall. They first ordered us to take off our shoelaces, our belts, to take out all valuables from our pockets, and Safet Ramadanovic, who was standing next to me, took out some money that he had on him, and the chief whose name I learned later on as being Krle, he said to him, "Cifut, you haven't brought us enough money. You will have to bring more to us. We have our methods."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, this name Cifut, is that a particular nickname? Does that have any particular significance?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It is a derogatory name for a person who likes money.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then what happened after this?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, we simply had to stand against the wall, and they started to beat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: While they were beating us, our faces were facing the wall, and I don't know how long it took. I remember the moment when I heard Kvocka's voice. He shouted all of a sudden, "Who brought Nusret Sivac to the camp?" At that moment, the guards stopped beating us and we turned around, and Kvocka came to Tomislav Stojakovic and Brane Bolta, who had taken us from Prijedor, and he told them, "Why have you brought Mr. Sivac here? We need his sister, (redacted), who used to work as a judge in the court in Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And after he said that, what happened?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Then Tomo Stojakvic who had brought us there asked him, "What am I going to do with him?" He said, "Wait a second. I'm going to see Mico, the boss. I'll ask him what to do."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that Tomo asked, "What am I going to do with him?" Whom did he ask that of?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He addressed that question to Miroslav Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you testified that he said, "Wait a second. I'm going to see Mico, the boss." Who said that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Kvocka said, "I'm going upstairs to see Mico, the boss, to see what we are supposed to do with him." I apologise. His name is actually Ranko Mijic. That is his full name.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: After several minutes, Kvocka came back and he said, "Mijic said that you should take him back to Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And is that what happened, you were taken back to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, that day when you saw Miroslav Kvocka in Omarska camp, do you recall what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was wearing a dark blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And do you recall anything else about what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: That's all I remember. Yes, and he also had a dark blue beret.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what kind of weapon, if any, he was carrying on that day?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He would typically carry the pump-action rifle, the so-called pump-action rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now I'd like to direct your attention to on or about the 23rd of June. Were you arrested on that date?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And by whom were you arrested on that date?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Again by the same individuals, by Ranko Kovacic, Bato.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you then taken to the SUP?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what other arrested persons, if any, did you see there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I saw Sifeta Susic there, together with Ago Sadikovic, and Dr. Osman Mahmuljin. Tesma Elezovic was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Ago Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him for very long.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was a Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his age, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was around 40 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was an employee of the security service, and he was working at the crime department.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also mentioned a Tesma Elezovic. Did you know her?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was her ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: She was a Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was her occupation, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: She was managing a restaurant on the Kozora Mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in the SUP on this day, did you also see a young boy being held there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was this young boy's name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Samir Malovcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his age?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Later on, while we were talking, he told us that he was thirteen and a half.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you know, what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was a Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, while you were held at the SUP, were you men and this young boy beaten there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They beat all the men, with the exception of Sifeta Susic, and Tesma Elezovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this young boy was also beaten?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then were the group of you taken to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The police van parked behind the restaurant, between the restaurant and the "white house." The first to get off was Sifeta Susic, and Tesma Elezovic, and they were taken away somewhere. Then from the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and english transcripts back part of the van they ordered to us get off. However, Dr. Osman Mahmuljin was in such bad shape that he couldn't get up. Then I and Ago Sadikovic and this young boy had to carry Dr. Osman out of the police van and lean him against the wall of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after you leaned him against the wall of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He couldn't stand and he simply fell to his knees.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened to you all after that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They started to beat us for a short while, and then we were facing the wall, and then someone said -- one of the guards said, "These have had enough for today. We won't beat them any longer today."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, when you first arrived at Omarska on this date and you were taken from the van, did you see anyone there that you recognised among the camp personnel?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I recognised again Milojica Kos, Krle, who was again the shift leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And on that occasion, what, if anything, did Krle say to you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. He said, "So you've come again but this time it's not by mistake."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, after these beatings had ended, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: To the garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And this garage was in what building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The garage was underneath the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held in this garage?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: For seven days.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see a man by the name of Muhamed Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: A Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you know, what political positions did he hold in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. He was president of the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he also held in this garage with you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his condition when you saw him in the garage?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was in a very bad state.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Judges what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was standing right next to the metal doors, to the left of the door. There were traces of mistreatment and beatings on his face. He was very sick. The inmates around him helped him to urinate, and he would urinate into a bottle that he had at his side, and I could see that there was blood in his urine.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, this first day that you were held in the garage, do you recall Muhamed Cehajic being called out of the garage?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, in the evenings.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you come to know the name or nickname of the person who called him out?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It was my first contact with that guard. He was short, well built. He had his sleeves rolled up as well as his trousers. He had fair hair, and he wore some strange red glasses.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And was he known by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I don't know, but we called him Zuti or the "yellow" one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you come to learn what shift he worked on?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I think in Ckalja's shift.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, what happened or what did you hear after this man called Muhamed Cehajic out?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: When Professor Cehajic went out, we could hear blows, screams, moans. We heard the blows. This went on I don't know exactly for how long. After awhile, the door was opened and the president of the municipality, Cehajic, appeared in the doorway with his head covered in blood, and he said, "They ordered me to collect a hundred German marks. If I don't do that, they'll kill me this evening."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to collect this 100 Deutschemarks?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: We didn't because we didn't have any on us, neither did the people we found in the garage when we arrived. But Dr. Osman Mahmuljin had a hundred German marks hidden somewhere, and he gave them to Muhamed Cehajic, and so he saved his life, the professor's life, that evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: After Muhamed Cehajic was given the money, did he then give it to someone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. He went outside, he left the garage, and again blows were heard outside, which means that he was beaten again, but after awhile he returned. Right close to the doorway he fell, and the detainees who were near the door helped him come in and led him to the place where he was before.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, during this seven days or so that you were held in the garage, was Muhamed Cehajic called out on other occasions?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Almost every day and every night.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when he would come back, what would be his condition?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Very, very bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he would come back, would you see fresh signs of beating?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. There were always fresh signs of beating. Towards the end of the time I was in the garage, they even tore up the jacket he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You've testified that 100 Deutschemarks was demanded of Muhamed Cehajic. During the time that you were in the garage, were demands made of other detainees for money or other valuables?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Almost every night.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what amounts of money or what valuables were demanded?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They demanded watches most, especially Seiko watches; German marks; US dollars; gold; and anything else of value.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it who made these demands?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Usually the guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would happen if you couldn't meet their demands?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, mostly they would take us out and beat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And on what shifts did these demands and these beatings occur?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Almost in all the shifts, but mostly in the shift whose leader was Mladjo Radic, Krkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, after about seven days in the garage, were you taken out for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you beaten during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you sign any kind of statement during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was any kind of statement read to you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, after this interrogation, were you held on the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Until about the second half of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: After that, were you able to get into Mujo's room and stay there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Until the 6th of August, when I was transferred to the camp in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, thinking back to the 10th of June when you were first taken to the Omarska camp, when you came to the camp did you see a flag of any sort flying at the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Very close to the garage there were the masts and on them was a large flag of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were brought back to the camp on about the 23rd of June and held in the camp thereafter, did you see this flag during that time period as well?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did. It was there throughout the period we stayed in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you some questions about camp personnel. You have testified that on the 10th of June, you saw Miroslav Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, from the time that you were taken back to Omarska on about the 23rd of June until 6 August, during that time period did you ever see Kvocka in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often did you see him in the camp during this time period?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: When I was on the pista, I would see him every second or third day. When I went to Mujo's room, I only saw him a couple of times when we went to the restaurant to eat.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, on these occasions when you saw Kvocka in the camp, where would he be when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Usually he would be standing in the corridor which led to the restaurant and near the door that led to the "glass house."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could please be provided with 3/77A.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at this for a moment, this diagram, to orient yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, first of all, just to be clear for the record, you talked about being held in the garage for seven days. Would you point to the area you called the garage?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It's this area here, A1.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you talked about be held in Mujo's room. Would you point to that area?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: This is, I think, A9.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the times that you would see Kvocka in the camp during this second period of time that you were held in the camp, you said you would see him in the corridor. Could you show the Judges where it is that you would see him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Once here in A13 where the steps led upstairs to where the interrogations took place, and once I saw him here too, in front of A15 and A16, in the area marked A13. Then I saw him once here in the area marked A22, in front of the area marked A14.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And this area marked A14, what was that area called?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The "glass house."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And the usher may take the exhibit back.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, during the times you saw him in Omarska, what would Kvocka be doing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Kvocka was usually with a soldier who was like his escort, who always stood behind his back. He was well built, with a short cut, and he would usually talk to someone.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what would he wear on these occasions when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He would be wearing a camouflage uniform, and with his pump-action rifle which he held like this, with gloves, leather gloves, black leather gloves with the fingers cut off on top, at the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, earlier you said that you saw him on the 10th of June in a blue or a dark blue camouflage uniform. The camouflage uniform you saw him in on these other occasions, was it also a dark blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: The times that you saw him in Omarska camp, what did you observe about the conduct of other camp personnel toward him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He had authority in relation to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was it you observed to make you say that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The guards looked up to him, treated him with respect, and also by the detainees with whom he stopped to talk.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have testified that you knew his wife's brothers. Did you ever see them in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were they held in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Usually in the "glass house."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Kvocka talking with any of them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. He would take one of them out and talk to him, precisely the area I have indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, when you saw him take one of them out and talk to this person, did you ever observe Kvocka ask anyone's permission to do this?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You've also testified about a man. You said you later learned his name was Krle, and his proper name was Kos.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you first learn that this man's nickname was Krle?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: When I was held at the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: From the detainees who had arrived before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was it they were able to tell you that this man's nickname was Krle?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I don't know, but among them was Muharem Murselovic, a man who was Krle's teacher in the catering school in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you said that you learned that his proper name was Kos. From whom did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: From Muharem Murselovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you describe this Krle as you saw him in Omarska in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, usually he was wearing olive-grey military trousers, and as a rule, he just wore an undervest, an athletic T-shirt. To me he looked well built. And he regularly carried a light machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what colour his hair was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I think it was brown. He always had a short cut with a kind of fringe, which was quite typical.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what his height was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: About 180, as far as I was able to judge. About 180, 185. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to judge about what age group he was in?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was young, I think, about 25. Anyway, between 20 and 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Omarska, how often would you see Krle?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: While I was at the pista, I would see him frequently. When I went to Mujo's room, then only when I went for meals or when we were taken out to spend a few minutes outside on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What areas of the camp would you see him in? Where would he be? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and english transcripts

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Most frequently in front of the entrance to the administration building, but I would also see him touring the guards at their posts around the administration building and over there near the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have testified that Krle was a shift commander. Did you come to understand the schedule of shifts at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that schedule?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They changed every 12 hours, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was it that you saw or heard that led you to the conclusion that Krle was a shift commander?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: All the things he did showed that he was coordinating, and he gave instructions to the guards who were around him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, were you ever present when he gave orders to the guards?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was not, but I could see it well from the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were held on the pista, if a person wanted to go from one area to another, who would they have to ask permission of?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They would have to ask permission from the guards who were usually there at the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when they asked permission of the guards, what would the guards tell them that they had to do?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: That they would have to ask the shift leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see who that shift leader was they would then go to?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: The shift leader was Krle, and then on another occasion Krkan, and also Ckalja.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion, while you were being held on the pista, when there were too many men to fit into the restaurant building for the night?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I do remember it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what happened on that occasion regarding the men who couldn't fit into the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Krle came and ordered all those who couldn't enter the restaurant and who were at the glass windows leading to the restaurant to line-up in this part of the pista between the restaurant and the "white house" and to be taken to sleep in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you one of those taken to sleep in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have mentioned two other shifts, Krkan's shift and Ckalja's shift. How would you characterise the treatment of detainees on all of these shifts?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: In all shifts, the prisoners were mistreated, called out, taken out. They wouldn't come back, which means that they were executed. But somehow in Krkan's shift, things were the worst.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you refer to this man Krkan, who is the man you're referring to? What's his proper name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Mladjo Radic, known as Krkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often did you see him while you were at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Very frequently while I was at the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when you saw him, where would he be?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He would also coordinate and talk to the guards, but most frequently he would be at the steps next to this large glass window, and through it he observed the prisoners on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I would ask that the exhibit that I have marked 3/13 [sic] be provided to the witness. I have copies for Your Honours. I believe that we have previously provided copies of this to the Defence, but if this copy could be shown to the Defence to ensure that we have. Your Honours, if I misspoke, it's 3/113, 113. If the witness could be shown that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you'd take a moment to look at that, and then if it could be placed on the ELMO. Now, you talked about seeing Krkan most frequently at the steps next to a large glass window where he was observing the prisoners. Could you show the Judges what area you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Ms. Hollis. I think there seems to be a technical problem with the ELMO. We have lost the picture, so we cannot see what you're talking about. It's still not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps while they're trying to correct that, we could go on with the questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that's a good suggestion, Ms. Hollis. You can ask that question later when the technicians repair the problem. So please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to this area where this large glass area was, what areas of the camp would you see Krkan in?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: As I told you, he would tour the guards' positions. He would go towards the"white house" or the hangar where the guards were stationed and where we, the detainees, were put up.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when you saw him, what we be doing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He would be giving instructions to the guards, who would then separate the detainees, those who had to go clean something or perform some other manual work in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you've referred to the shift as Krkan's shift. What was his position, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was a shift leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see or hear to lead you to conclude that he was a shift leader?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I could tell it by the way he behaved. The guards had to obey him and had to comply with his orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you come to recognise any of the guards who worked on Krkan's shift?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And today, do you recall the names or nicknames of any of those guards?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I remember certain nicknames such as Pop, Sole, Paspalj, Savic. I've forgotten others.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "Paspalj," to your knowledge is that a nickname or a real name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I think it's a surname.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And "Savic," to your knowledge, that a nickname or a proper name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It's a surname.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, this guard Pop and Sole, where would you say them most often in the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Usually they would be standing across from the entrance to the Mujo's room, but very often he would also come to the area leading up to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "very often he would also come to the area leading up to the administration building," who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Pop, about Pop, the guards, and Sole.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And the guards Paspalj and Savic, where would you see them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Most often they would be at the entrance near the staircase leading to the restaurant and the administration building where the interrogations were conducted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have testified that Krkan's shift stood out among the shifts as perhaps being the worst shift. What would happen on his shift to lead you to say that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: During the time when Krkan's shift was on duty, most of the people would be taken out, mistreated, beaten up, valuables would be seized such as watches, gold, money. They did it openly and in a very rough way. They didn't try to hide it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Krkan himself engage in any of this conduct such as calling people out?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He would sometimes call people out. He would do so from the area in front of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: In front of the entrance to what?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: To the administration building where the interrogations were conducted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, these people who were called out, did all of them come back after these call-outs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Some came back and some came back in bags or blankets.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you said some came back in blankets or bags. What would be their condition?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They would be either badly beaten up or simply dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, we spoke a little bit earlier about Krle's shift. Did you come to recognise any of the guards on Krle's shift?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, one guard in particular, who would very often be in the area between the restaurant and the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Today can you recall the names or nicknames of any of those guards?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It's hard for me to recall. Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you've also talked about Ckalja's shift. How did you come to know who Ckalja was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I first came to know Ckalja, unfortunately, in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was it that you knew that this particular person was called Ckalja?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: From the detainees who had arrived before me and who had spent some time on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how often would you see Ckalja in the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Likewise, very often. He walked around the camp more often than other shift leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you come to recognise guards who worked on his shift?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I came to know Zeljko Marmat "Zuti" and a person by the surname of Pavlic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Drago Prcac in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how often would you see him in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: At the beginning, not very often. However, later on I saw him on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in what areas of the camp would you see him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, he too would come down and tour the rooms where the detainees were put up, but most often I would see him in the room which had an antenna on one of its windows, an antenna that served to establish radio communications. That room was above Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would see Prcac in the camp, what would he be doing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but in the month of July, he carried some kind of lists, carried them around, and sometimes he would read out names from those lists and sometimes he would give them to the guards to read out the names. People who were taken out from Mujo's room, from the pista, or from the garage would be then lined up on the area in front of the building, in front of the pista. Then a kind of selection would take place. Some people would move from the garage to the hangar and the other way round.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion in Omarska where you saw Drago Prcac with a cameraman that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. It was Slavisa Djukanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw Prcac and this other man on that occasion, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They were filming something around the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in what areas of the camp did you see them filming?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: At the beginning, they were in the area between the restaurant and the "white house," and after that they moved to the area between the hangar and the "white house," and after that they went to the area behind the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was Drago Prcac's position in the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: According to what I know, he was the deputy commander of the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see or hear in the camp to lead you to conclude that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: At that time, that is, from mid-July or thereabouts, for all the work that needed to be done, and when I say that I'm referring to the permissions for transfer of detainees from one room to another, a guard had to be approached. Then the guard would usually say that he had to go and see Drago Prcac and to ask if that could be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion when Mujo wanted to bring a prisoner from the "white house" into Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did Mujo have to do to bring this prisoner from the "white house" into Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He asked a guard whether he could go to the "white house," because during the day a person by the name of Smail Duratovic, who had been taken Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and english transcripts out from the restaurant, was beaten up there, and he was in Mujo's room together with his father. One of the women passed on a message saying that if Mujo doesn't come to fetch Smail Duratovic in the"white house," that the latter would be liquidated during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, from whom did Mujo have to get permission to bring Smail to Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: First he had to approach the guard who was there in the area outside Mujo's room, and the guard said, "You have to wait. I have to go and ask Prcac about that."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this transfer allowed?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When this man came into Mujo's room, could you see what his condition was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was in a poor condition. He had countless injuries on him. He had been placed in a large truck tyre which was then set on fire, so his body was charred, and you could clearly see burns on his face and his arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn that he had been placed in this large truck tyre?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: That is what he told us. And the women who were in the restaurant could also see this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he tell you when it was that he had been put in this large truck tyre?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It happened some time in the afternoon. He was going for lunch, he was among the last ones in the group, and he was recognised by one of the guards, and the guard took him out and did it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would see Drago Prcac in Omarska camp, what would he be wearing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Most often he would be wearing a blue police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Nenad Lakic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He used to work with us at the security service in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was his relationship, if any, to Slavica Lakic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He was related to her. Slavica's husband, Bosko, is Nenad Lakic's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were held in Omarska, did you ever see Nenad Lakic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And do you know what his duties were there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: He worked as an interrogator upstairs in the interrogation rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you ever see Slavica Lakic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you know, what were her duties in the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: She was working in the administration of the camp. She's a typist by occupation, so she was probably typing records of interrogations of detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, do we know if the problem with the ELMO has been corrected? Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think it has been corrected. At least we can see the photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, earlier you talked about seeing Krkan in this window area. Could you show the Judges what window area you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: It is this area here, A21, above A21.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And that window area was what? Was that the stairwell up to the first floor of the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. These stairs led to the rooms where interrogations took place, and the area here had very large glass panes on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you're pointing to that clear area above A21; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the area that I would see Krkan very often, but I also saw him at these windows here, at the windows of the interrogation rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you're pointing to windows on the first floor of the restaurant building on the side that the garage is on?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you also said that two of the guards that worked on Krkan's shift would often be in front of the administration building. Can you show us on this exhibit where those guards would be? You talked about Paspalj and Savic.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: They would usually be here near these pillars.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you're talking about the support pillars for the canopy over the administration building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, if the witness could also be provided with Exhibit 104, please. Now, you also -- could you take a moment to look at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: That could also be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you also talked about two other guards, Pop and Sole, that you said were located somewhere near the entrance to Mujo's rooms. Could you show the Judges where their normal location was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: At this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And you're pointing to an area that is across from a door on the model on the garage side of the restaurant building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. So that they could control both the garage and Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any sort of vehicle or structure that was normally there in that area?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, there was. A van would always be parked here in this area, which had no doors on it. And there was an area covered with some branches which was supposed to protect the guards from rain and sunshine.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when you would see these two guards near this kombi and this covered area, what would they be doing there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, most often they would provoke people, verbally abuse them. They would cock their rifles. They would provoke us most while we were lining up in this area here, as we were leaving Mujo's room while going out for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you look at the photograph, that would be the area to the left of the door in the middle of that side of the building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is where we would be lined up, in front of Mujo's room, against this wall here. We would be lined up in groups of 30 to go to have our meals.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you also talked about seeing Drago Prcac at the window of a room that had an antenna sticking out of the room. Where was that room located?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: That room was located above the room where we were, that is, above Mujo's room. Here in this area roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: So those would be the windows above and to the left of the doorway that you pointed to?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to move to a series of incidents that I will ask the witness about. Do you want to commence the incidents now or do you want to commence them tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time do you need approximately, Ms. Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I have another half hour to 45 minutes with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, it is better that we adjourn for the day and continue tomorrow morning, except that we have to be here again at 4.00, but not the witness, of course. Mr. Usher, could you please help the witness out of the courtroom. Witness, we will see you again here tomorrow at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4.00 we will be here again. It will be a public session, so we will be wearing robes.
